newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX jumps to second successive high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX jumps to second successive high.

text.p: The Hungarian bourse continued to set new highs on Monday helped by the dollar's gain against the forint and by fresh capital reaching the market, traders said.

"It was predictable that the dollar's rise would have a beneficial impact on the market," said Kalman Schuszter of New York Broker Budapest. "In addition, new capital arrived, probably from the Czech market...still, the size of the rise was surprising."

The BUX index finished unofficially at 6,139.09 points, up 120.98 points, a two percent rise following on the heels of Friday's 1.50 percent gain. Traders said the BUX futures market was also trading higher by between 150 and 200 points.
The forint has substantially weakened against the dollar, following the dollar/mark cross, and at midday at stood at 183.85 to the dollar, compared to Friday's close of 182.35/40.
Traders said they saw foreigners as the main buying force on the market on which they detected signs of overheating.
"With the exception of TVK foreigners were the dominant buyers of blue chip stocks," said Attila Hunyadi of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz.

"There's fresh money on the market, possibly with new investors who have not invested here yet," Hunyadi said, adding he saw signs of certain new investors beginning to build a portfolio of Hungarian stocks.

He added the market may be rising too far too quickly and this might take its toll in the near future. "The market has overreacted slightly, and although there might be some correction, the trend is upward."
TVK was among the day's strong gainers, rallying 100 forints to finish at 2,870.
Another trader said earlier that TVK was rallying on investor belief that the paper will maintain its level when it begins to trade without dividend coupons on Tuesday.

On Monday, pharmaceuticals Richter Gedeon rallied to a new record of 15,650 forints before retreating to close at 15,575, up 375. Chemicals BorsodChem was also in record breaking form, reaching 7,000 forints. It closed at 6,955 forints, up 255.
Machinery company Mezogep grabbed attention by an agency cross for 280,000 shares, 3.53 percent of the company's capital, at 2,100 forints. Mezogep closed steady at 2,250.
Some analysts said they saw the Budapest bourse's near term upside potential more limited as foreigners might find the Polish market more exciting because of fresh investment opportunities there.
"In the short-term, Poland will probably drain quite a lot of money for the two big upcoming share issues," said Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London.
The Hungarian market was more expensive than the Czech and the Polish markets, but the Hungarian bourse's longer-term outlook was positive, he added.

"People generally expect the BUX index to be between 6,500 and 7,500 by the end of the year," Sitanyi said. "They agree there's still upside (potential) but they generally believe this would come in the autumn."
In the autumn second quarter earnings figures will have already been on the market, while Hungary's will proceed with fresh share offers, market participants said.
